framework.title: 2024 Climate Act siting reforms (Chapter 239 of the Acts of 2024)
framework.summary: The law created a single consolidated local permit for small clean-energy projects (generation under 25 MW, storage under 100 MWh) with a 12-month municipal decision deadline, and moved larger projects to a consolidated Energy Facilities Siting Board permit. It was approved Nov. 20, 2024.

framework.title: 225 CMR 29.00: consolidated local permit for small clean energy infrastructure
framework.summary: DOER's final rule, promulgated Feb. 27, 2026, lets towns accept consolidated local permit applications starting July 1, 2026 and requires them to accept them by Oct. 1, 2026. Towns must decide within 12 months of a complete application; if they do not, the permit is constructively approved subject to standard conditions.

sources.title: 225 CMR 29.00 final regulation (DOER)

framework.title: Oct. 1, 2026 deadline and DOER application guideline
framework.summary: As of Oct. 1, 2026 every city and town must accept consolidated local permit applications using DOER's required forms (pre-filing checklist, application, completeness checklist and decision form). DOER's guideline on the application took effect that day.

framework.title: Energy Facilities Siting Board rules (980 CMR 13.00, 14.00, 16.00)
framework.summary: EFSB rules on consolidated permits for large facilities, de novo review of local permit applications, and pre-filing engagement were published Feb. 27, 2026. Under 225 CMR 29.00, a town that lacks capacity may ask the EFSB, within 60 days of receiving an application, to review it instead.

framework.title: DOER model consolidated permitting bylaw
framework.summary: DOER's May 22, 2026 model bylaw shows towns how to fold the 225 CMR 29.00 process into local zoning. DOER states that adopting it is not required for the regulation to apply.

framework.title: DOER model zoning bylaws for solar and battery storage
framework.summary: DOER issued final model zoning bylaws for solar photovoltaic installations and for battery energy storage systems in August 2026, after releasing drafts in October 2025. Towns may adopt them as written or modify them, and DOER recommends review by municipal counsel.

framework.title: Attorney General review of town moratoria (G.L. c. 40A, s. 3)
framework.summary: Since the SJC's 2022 Tracer Lane II decision, the Attorney General's Municipal Law Unit has disapproved town moratoria on solar and battery storage, including Carver (2022), Ware (2023), Northfield (2024), and Blandford, Becket and Worthington (2026), for lacking a specific health, safety or welfare justification. The office has approved BESS zoning that regulates rather than prohibits, such as Wilbraham, Hadley and Petersham.

framework.title: Duxbury Energy Storage v. Duxbury ZBA (Land Court)
framework.summary: On June 23, 2025 the Land Court held that a standalone battery storage facility is protected by the solar provision of G.L. c. 40A, s. 3 and annulled the town's denial. Towns have cited it as a reason they cannot ban BESS outright.

sources.title: Climate Case Chart: Duxbury Energy Storage, LLC v. Town of Duxbury ZBA

framework.title: Sunpin Energy Services v. Petersham ZBA (Supreme Judicial Court)
framework.summary: On July 14, 2026 the SJC annulled Petersham's denial of a solar special permit, holding that a town may deny a protected solar project only where needed to protect public health, safety or welfare. The case went back to the zoning board.
